answer:
Use the prebuilt **`FunctionAgent`** from the agent workflow module. The agents guide shows it in a short example:

"from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import FunctionAgent" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]

The example passes a plain Python function as a tool, along with an LLM and a system prompt:

"agent = FunctionAgent(" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]

The tool is an ordinary function with a docstring describing what it does:

"Useful for multiplying two numbers." [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]

The tool's name and description matter because the LLM uses them to decide when and how to call the tool: "the tool selected (and the arguments written for that tool) rely strongly on the **tool name** and **description**" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/tools.md]

The introduction also names `FunctionAgent` as one of the pre-built options: "you can use our pre-built agentic workflows like `FunctionAgent`" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/understanding/agent/index.md]

The excerpts I have are truncated, so I don't know the rest of the example, such as how to run the agent or pass it a query. Check the full agents guide for those details.
